deck_title: Synthetic Conference Oral Deck — Adaptive Closed-Loop Insulin Delivery in Inpatient Corticosteroid Hyperglycemia
authors: Synthetic Study Investigators · Department of Endocrinology & Biomedical Engineering

slides.headline: Closed-Loop Automated Insulin Delivery Doubles Time-in-Range During Inpatient Corticosteroid Therapy
slides.subtitle: A Synthetic Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (N = 280)
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome colleagues. Today I share synthetic benchmark results evaluating automated closed-loop insulin delivery in hospitalized non-ICU adults receiving high-dose systemic glucocorticoids.

slides.headline: High-Dose Glucocorticoids Trigger Severe Afternoon Hyperglycemia Missed by Sliding-Scale Insulin
bullets: Prednisolone >= 30 mg/day induces acute postprandial hepatic & peripheral insulin resistance
Conventional basal-bolus regimens achieve < 45% glucose time-in-range (70–180 mg/dL)
Reactive correction boluses increase nocturnal hypoglycemia (< 70 mg/dL)
slides.footnote: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE DATA · Glycemic target range 70–180 mg/dL
slides.speaker_notes: Highlight the characteristic afternoon surge between 12:00 and 20:00 driven by morning prednisolone dosing, where standard weight-based regimens lag physiological insulin demand.

slides.headline: 280 Medical Ward Patients Were Randomized 1:1 to CGM-Guided Closed-Loop vs Basal-Bolus Care

stages.detail: Adults on >= 30 mg prednisolone-eq with 2 BG > 180 mg/dL across 6 hospitals.
Stratified by prior T2D diagnosis and steroid dose tier (n=140 per arm).
MPC closed-loop pump + CGM q5m vs masked-CGM standard basal-bolus.
% Time-in-Range (70–180 mg/dL) over days 1–10 with safety hypoglycemia audit.

slides.speaker_notes: Walk left-to-right: masked CGM in the control arm ensured unbiased sensor capture of both hyperglycemia and asymptomatic nocturnal hypoglycemia.

slides.headline: Closed-Loop Delivery Increased Time-in-Range From 41.8% to 72.4% Without Raising Hypoglycemia
bullets: Mean difference +30.6 percentage points (95% CI +26.4 to +34.8; P < 0.0001)
Mean sensor glucose fell from 204 mg/dL to 156 mg/dL
Time < 70 mg/dL remained low in both arms (0.6% vs 1.4%; P = 0.03)
slides.footnote: SYNTHETIC PRIMARY ENDPOINT · Error bars denote 95% CIs
slides.speaker_notes: Emphasize the +30.6% absolute gain in time-in-range—roughly 7.3 additional hours per day in euglycemia—achieved alongside lower hypoglycemia.

slides.headline: Glycemic Control Improved Consistently Across Secondary Safety and Nursing Workload Metrics
slides.speaker_notes: Point out row 1 and row 4: severe hyperglycemia above 250 mg/dL dropped nearly five-fold while ward point-of-care capillary checks dropped by 3.1 per day.

slides.headline: Conclusions & Honest Study Limitations
bullets: Automated closed-loop insulin safely adapts to dynamic corticosteroid-induced insulin resistance on general wards
Achieved +30.6% higher Time-in-Range while cutting capillary fingerstick burden by 72%
LIMITATION: Open-label device wear; excluded ICU vasopressor patients and end-stage dialysis
NEXT STEP: Cost-effectiveness & hospital length-of-stay powered pragmatic rollout
slides.footnote: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE DECK FOR SKILL VALIDATION ONLY
slides.speaker_notes: Close transparently by noting open-label device constraints and inviting questions on ward nursing implementation.
